# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–4 (Complete and Final – Updated 62)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) just after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; narrative extends into future years; present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford; Also: Chiswick Mall (Miss Pinkerton's academy), Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, playground with tree and broken glass on wall, Bedford tavern
- **Current Setting Details**: River crossing at Gulton and Quenwick; forge with chalked crooked sun on wall; wind from water with salt and tar smell; gulls quarreling over fish heads by steps; smoke from chimneys lying flat over fields; frost silvering hedges overnight; turnip cart passing well; light going early as spring approaches; children chasing hoop down lane; road all ruts and puddles after thaw; market town of Bryngate; hill farms of Coldcombe and Mirecombe; bees humming in lavender behind parsonage; bell for vespers ringing thinly across roofs; rain threatening but holding off; front room on second floor with chintz tent hung round with rich India pattern and double calico of tender rose-colour, featherbed with two pillows; back drawing-room with piano situated in darkness; schoolyard with tree where Arabian Nights may be read in solitude

## Main Characters

**Dorothea and Will Ladislaw (Married)**
- Engaged after Will's return to Middlemarch; now married with infant son
- **Family Reconciliation**: Initial opposition resolved; established pattern of two yearly visits to Grange; Dorothea and Will's cousins enjoy playing with visiting children
- **Sir James's Opposition**: Never ceased regarding second marriage as mistake
- **Dorothea's Life Assessment**: Acts not ideally beautiful but mixed result of young, noble impulse; finely touched spirit with fine issues though not widely visible; full nature spent in channels with no great name; effect incalculably diffusive

**Mary Garth and Fred Garth (Married)**
- **Present Status**: Inhabit Stone Court; seen in white-haired placidity at open window
- **Marriage Achievement**: Solid mutual happiness; Fred becomes distinguished county farmer; produces work on "Cultivation of Green Crops and the Economy of Cattle-Feeding" winning agricultural meeting congratulations
- **Fred's Development**: Remains steady; told Mary happiness half owing to Farebrother; never wholly free from misled hopefulness but gradually saved enough to become Stone Court owner
- **Children**: Three boys only; youngest resembles grandfather

**Rebecca Sharp (Miss Becky)**
- **Age and Background**: Age nineteen; father was artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy—clever, prone to debt and tavern, beat wife and daughter when drunk, died after third delirium tremens; mother was French opera-girl; claims descent from noble Entrechats family of Gascony
- **Appearance**: Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large, odd, attractive eyes; dressed in white with bare shoulders; white slender fingers
- **Accomplishments**: Speaks French with purity and Parisian accent; skilled musician and linguist; clever artist; sings better than Amelia
- **Departure from Chiswick**: Threw Dixonary at Miss Jemima; obtained governess position with Sir Pitt Crawley's family after months-long battle to cancel indentures; Miss Pinkerton recommended her stating "I cannot find fault with Miss Sharp's conduct except to myself; must allow her talents and accomplishments are of high order"
- **Character**: Had dismal precocity of poverty; determined to make connected plans for future; never blushed since age eight when caught stealing jam by godmother; capable of calculated charm and intimacy
- **Crisp Affair**: Reverend Mr. Crisp, fresh from Oxford and curate to Vicar Flowerdew of Chiswick, fell in love and proposed in intercepted note; **rumor claims** tart-woman hinted great deal more than public knowledge
- **At Sedley Household**: Invited by friend Miss Sedley for week before governess duties; Amelia showed her rooms, books, piano, dresses, necklaces, braces, laces; insisted Rebecca accept white cornelian and turquoise rings, sprigged muslin, white Cashmere shawl; won over entire household through charming behavior
- **Regarding Joseph Sedley**: Upon learning of India shawls, Rebecca determined "If Mr. Joseph Sedley is rich and unmarried, why should I not marry him?"
- **Meeting Joseph**: Went downstairs with arm round Amelia's waist; dressed in white with bare shoulders; at dinner, at chili, cried "Water, for Heaven's sake, water!" and made comical air about Arabian Nights
- **Joseph's Initial Reaction**: Did not visit house nor mention Miss Rebecca's name for two or three days following dinner
- **Winning Over Household**: Laughed at Mr. Sedley's jokes with cordiality; interested Mrs. Blenkinsop in raspberry-jam preserving; called Sambo "Sir" and "Mr. Sambo"; charmed both Drawing Room and Servants' Hall; by day ten, on footing of considerable familiarity with family
- **Hand Pressure and Rekindling**: Gave Joseph gentle pressure with little hand, drew it back frightened, looked in his face; Joseph's heart thumped; Joseph thought "I exactly begin to feel as I did at Dumdum with Miss Cutler"
- **Intimate Evening**: Left alone with Joseph in drawing-room while Amelia and George Osborne went to piano; Rebecca occupied knitting green silk purse; conversation established great confidence and intimacy; asked Joseph about purse recipient; Joseph began eloquent speech "O Miss Sharp, how--" but stopped when music ended, blushed, blew nose in agitation
- **Joseph's Meditations**: Lay awake thinking of marrying her; concluded "It's evident the poor devil's in love with me"; thought "I might go farther, and fare worse"
- **Next Morning**: Rebecca employed on knitting work when Joseph's buggy arrived; blushed as she bent fair ringlets over knitting; Joseph presented nosegays of flowers from Covent Garden Market to each young woman; Rebecca exclaimed "O heavenly, heavenly flowers!" holding to bosom, casting eyes to ceiling; looked for billet-doux but found no letter
- **Pine-apple Incident**: Rebecca said she had never tasted pine and longed beyond everything to taste one; Joseph left alone with Rebecca who resumed work with green silk and shining needles
- **Current Moment**: Rebecca refuses Joseph's request to sing, citing low spirits; asks him to help finish green silk purse; Joseph seated tete-a-tete looking at her with killing expression, hands bound in web of green silk

**Joseph Sedley**
- **Position and Background**: In East India Company's Civil Service; collector of Boggley Wollah for about eight years; caught liver complaint and returned to Europe; does not live with family but has own lodgings like gay young bachelor
- **Appearance and Habits**: Very stout, puffy man in buckskins and Hessian boots with immense neckcloths, red striped waistcoat, apple green coat with steel buttons; drives horses in Park, dines at fashionable taverns, frequents theatres, appears at opera; extremely talkative in man's society
- **Indulgences**: Contented himself with bottle of claret besides Madeira at dinner; ate couple plates of strawberries and cream and twenty-four little rout cakes; drank fitting quantity of port-wine tete-a-tete with George Osborne during thunderstorm evening
- **Cowardice**: Nearly cried with vexation at father's joke about ordering elephant from Exeter 'Change
- **Escape**: Slipped away on pointed toes of his boots to see Forty Thieves and Miss Decamp's dance without waking father
- **Prediction**: Destined to be prey to woman as father goes on 'Change daily

**Miss Amelia Sedley**
- **Character**: Pupil at Miss Pinkerton's; happy, handsome, seventeen years old; loves Rebecca like sister; natural infirmity of tears; match-maker at heart
- **Betrothal**: Bred up by parents for purpose of marrying George Osborne; banns read in respective families for ten years; appeared to fall in love with George Osborne at single instant when he asked her for music
- **Regarding Rebecca**: Discovered a million of virtues in Rebecca which she had not perceived at Chiswick; warmed into most tender friendship in course of few days' constant intercourse
- **Music and Affection**: Went with George Osborne to piano in back drawing-room during thunderstorm evening; put hand into his for guidance among chairs and ottomans; writing to twelve dearest friends at Chiswick Mall when Joseph arrived next morning; regards Dobbin's friendship with George as reason to like him

**George Osborne**
- **Background**: Sedley's godson; family friend for twenty-three years; received silver cup at six weeks old; received coral with gold whistle and bells at six months; regularly "tipped" at Christmas; thrashed by Joseph Sedley when hobbadehoy
- **Character and Feelings**: Clever artist; did not seem least disappointed at Vauxhall cancellation; felt extraordinary, almost irresistible impulse to seize Amelia in arms and kiss her; hinted he should like to sit in dark during piano performance; somehow already present at Russell Square when Joseph arrived next morning
- **Betrothal**: Bred up by parents for purpose of marrying Amelia; banns read in respective families for ten years; appeared to fall in love with Amelia at single instant
- **Character Assessment**: Though a little chap, had very high popularity among Swishtail youth; said of Dobbin "After all, it's not his fault that his father's a grocer"; his opinion received with great applause
- **Recent Appearance**: Met Dobbin at the Bedford tavern and told him Miss Amelia was come home and they were all bent on going out for night's pleasuring; mentioned Mrs. Sedley had forgiven Osborne breaking the punch-bowl at child's party seven years ago
- **Regarding Dobbin**: Amelia likes him as friend and champion of George, caring nothing about his complexion or awkwardness

**William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Background**: Son of merchant/grocer; father keeps shop "Figs & Rudge" on Thames Street, City
- **School Experience at Doctor Swishtail's Seminary**: Giant amongst boys, downcast and stupefied appearance, dog's-eared primer, tight corduroys; incapable of acquiring Latin rudiments; continually "taken down" by small boys; mercilessly bullied by entire school; corduroys sewn up, bed-strings cut, buckets and benches upset to break his shins, parcels of paternal soap and candles sent to him, subject of endless jesting; bore everything patiently, entirely dumb and miserable; called "Figs" as nickname of reproach
- **Defense of George Osborne**: While reading Arabian Nights under tree in playground, witnessed Cuff beating small boy instructed to purchase rum-shrub; boy's foot slipped, bottle broken, shrub spilt, pantaloons damaged; Dobbin sprang up and cried "Hold off, Cuff; don't bully that child any more; or I'll--"; previously had threatened Cuff with leaden inkstand when latter attempted to strike him for refusing to write to "old Mother Figs," saying "Don't strike, or I'll THMASH you" with such wickedness that Cuff backed down; after that Cuff never meddled personally with Dobbin though always spoke of him with contempt behind his back
- **The Famous Fight**: Young Osborne told Dobbin that Cuff was licking him for breaking a bottle of milk; Dobbin said "I'll give you the worst thrashing you ever had in your life" in reply to Cuff's sentence; Cuff's astonishment was immense at proposed rencontre. Fought thirteen rounds total. Initial rounds: scientific Cuff planted contemptuous blows with light gaiety as if at ball, floored Dobbin three times running; each fall brought cheers and offers of knees to conqueror. Round 4 onwards: Dobbin, all limbs quivering and nostrils breathing rage, determined to commence engagement by charge of his own; being left-handed, brought that arm into action, hit out with all his might once at Cuff's left eye and once on his beautiful Roman nose. Figs's left made terrific play during rest of combat. By round 6, almost as many fellows shouting "Go it, Figs" as "Go it, Cuff." By round 12, Cuff was all abroad, lost all presence of mind and power of attack or defence; Figs calm as quaker with pale face, eyes shining open, great cut on underlip bleeding profusely, giving fierce and ghastly air. Round 13 (final): Cuff came up full of pluck but quite reeling and groggy; Figs put in his left as usual on adversary's nose and sent him down for last time. All boys set up shout for Figs that brought Dr. Swishtail out of study. Doctor threatened to flog Figs violently; Cuff, washing his wounds, stood up and said "It's my fault, sir--not Figs'--not Dobbin's. I was bullying a little boy; and he served me right." Speech saved Dobbin from whipping and got Cuff back all his ascendancy over boys
- **Character Change**: In consequence of victory, his character rose prodigiously in estimation of all schoolfellows; name "Figs," byword of reproach, became respectable and popular nickname; voted low to sneer at Dobbin about accident of birth; "Old Figs" grew to be name of kindness and endearment; sneak of usher jeered at him no longer
- **School Letter**: Young Osborne wrote home describing fight, telling mother Dobbin licked Cuff so Cuff is now Only Second Cock, fight was about him, and that since Dobbin fought for him she ought to buy her Tea and Sugar at his father's

**Mr. Cuff** [School Years]
- **Position and Character**: Great chief and dandy of Swishtail Seminary; unquestioned king of school; smuggled wine; fought town-boys; had ponies for riding home Saturdays; owned top-boots for hunting holidays; possessed gold repeater; took snuff like Doctor; attended Opera; rumored Doctor himself feared him
- **Bullying Behavior**: Despised "Figs" (Dobbin) most, abused and sneered at him constantly; forced other boys to black his shoes, toast his bread, fag out; beat small boy over rum-shrub errand; attempted to strike Dobbin but backed down when threatened with inkstand; thereafter spoke of Dobbin with contempt behind his back but never meddled personally with him again
- **After Defeat**: Regained all his ascendancy through magnanimous speech acknowledging fault; now Only Second Cock

## Minor Characters and Events
- **Vauxhall Plan**: Thunderstorm on evening appointed for Vauxhall party prevented attendance; young people remained at home and declared themselves rather glad of storm than otherwise
- **Background Characters**: Miss Pinkerton, Miss Jemima, Mrs. Blenkinsop, Sambo, Reverend Mr. Crisp, Mr. and Mrs. Sedley, Doctor Swishtail, Orlwood family members, Wexwood family members, Corrett family members, Hollwood family members as previously noted
- **Supporting Details**: Young Osborne's letter home (incomplete, ends mid-sentence); punch-bowl incident at child's party seven years prior; milk bottle broken by young Osborne incident at school
